content: Mumps is an acute viral illness that spreads through respiratory droplets and saliva. Several studies conducted in China have indicated that acupuncture may be beneficial for children suffering from mumps. However, the available literature on the potential benefits or harms of acupuncture for mumps has not been systematically reviewed. The objective of this review was to evaluate the efficacy and safety of acupuncture as a treatment for children with mumps. To achieve this, a comprehensive search was conducted across multiple databases, including CENTRAL (up to Issue 11, 2014), MEDLINE (from 1950 to November 2014), EMBASE (from 1974 to December 2014), CINAHL (from 1981 to December 2014), AMED (from 1985 to December 2014), the Chinese BioMedical Literature Database (CBM, from 1979 to November 2014), China National Knowledge Infrastructure (CNKI, from 1979 to November 2014), Chinese Technology Periodical Database (CTPD, from 1989 to November 2014), and the Wanfang database (from 1982 to November 2014). Additionally, several journals were manually searched from their first issue to the most recent issue. The review focused on randomized controlled trials that compared acupuncture with placebo acupuncture, no treatment, Chinese medicine, Western medicine, or other interventions for mumps. The definition of acupuncture included both traditional and contemporary forms, regardless of the type of stimulation used (e.g., body acupuncture, electroacupuncture, scalp acupuncture, fire acupuncture, hand acupuncture, fine needle acupuncture, or moxibustion). Two independent reviewers extracted data for this analysis. However, no studies met the inclusion criteria for this updated review. As a result, no trials were included in the analysis. In conclusion, due to the lack of eligible studies, no definitive conclusions can be drawn regarding the efficacy or safety of acupuncture for treating mumps in children. Further high-quality research is necessary to address this gap in evidence.
